_README: MARKER-ONLY. Never fetched by the student's browser until a teacher/marker PDF is generated. Never render any of this on the student-facing page. See CLAUDE.md section 5's assessment-security amendment.

markingScheme.criterion: Quotes the Spanish words of one real task from their own Record (e.g. 'Nosotros somos', 'la chica alta') that they got wrong or needed two tries for.
markingScheme.accept: Any task in the student's own Record with Tries 2 or Right = No; if the Record is perfect, any task from it. Accents not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: Describing a rule in general with no task or Spanish words taken from their Record.

markingScheme.criterion: States the correct rule behind that task (gusta for one thing or a verb, gustan for several things; regular -ar endings -o/-as/-a/-amos/-an; quisiera for polite ordering; a Spain vs Latin America difference such as patatas/papas, zumo/jugo, camarero/mesero, coger/tomar).
markingScheme.accept: Any correct rule that fits the quoted task, in English or Spanish, in the student's own words.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'I got it wrong' or 'it changes' with no stated reason or pattern.

markingScheme.criterion: Writes one new, correct Spanish example that follows the stated rule.
markingScheme.accept: Any grammatically correct Unit 1 example (minor accent slips allowed if the form is clear), different from the quoted task.
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeating the quoted task, or a new example with a wrong verb form or ending.

markingScheme.criterion: Who and where: family members with a correct possessive (mi/mis/nuestro/nuestra...) and a correct estar sentence for where they are (estamos en la cocina).
markingScheme.accept: e.g. 'Mis padres y mi hermano están en casa'. Accents optional.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'Mi padres', or ser used for location ('somos en la cocina').

markingScheme.criterion: Likes: at least one correct 'me gusta + singular thing/verb' AND one correct 'me gustan + plural things'.
markingScheme.accept: e.g. 'Me gusta la pizza' and 'Me gustan los churros'.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'Me gusta los tacos' or 'Me gustan el café' (verb not matching the thing liked).

markingScheme.criterion: Verb and polite order plus English line: one correct regular -ar verb form (cenamos, cocina, desayuno...) AND a polite 'Quisiera ... por favor', AND the English line correctly explains choosing gusta vs gustan by whether what follows is singular/a verb or plural.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct -ar form; any quisiera sentence; a correct gusta/gustan explanation.
markingScheme.insufficient: Wrong ending ('nosotros ceno'), 'Quiero...' as the polite order, or an explanation that does not mention singular vs plural.

criteria.source: = the Explain question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: None of the three analytic points achieved: no real task quoted from the Record, no correct rule, and no correct new example.
Achieves only ONE of the three: quotes a real task from their Record OR states a correct rule OR gives a correct new example.
Achieves TWO of the three analytic points.
Quotes a real task from their own Record, states the correct rule, and gives a correct new Spanish example — all three analytic points present.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: None of the three analytic points achieved: no correct possessive + estar sentence, no correct gusta/gustan pair, and no correct -ar verb, polite quisiera order and gusta/gustan explanation.
Achieves only ONE of the three analytic points.
Achieves TWO of the three analytic points.

Correct possessive and estar sentence, a correct gusta and gustan pair, and a correct -ar verb with a polite quisiera order plus an accurate gusta/gustan explanation — all three analytic points present.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across BOTH the Explain and Apply answers together — independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks in use_of_evidence and spanish_use above.

levels.descriptor: Too unclear or incomplete for the meaning to be followed reliably.
Main meaning understandable, but organisation, vocabulary or precision cause some difficulty.
Clear and logical, uses Unit 1 vocabulary, and is easy to follow. Minor spelling or accent slips that do not harm meaning are not penalised.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply). Award marks point-by-point using each question's markingScheme: each point is worth the marks stated and is independent unless it names a dependsOn point (award it only if that earlier point was also awarded). use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain scheme's 3 points and spanish_use's 3 marks ARE the Apply scheme's 3 points; award each set once, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers. The Knowledge Check is ADAPTIVE (levels L1-L5): each student answers 5 one-mark items pitched at their level, so copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy (out of 5) and do not penalise a lower level; the level path is printed in the PDF. Use the student's logged Record (nivel/tarea/respuesta/correcto/intentos) to verify any task they quote. Students are true beginners (A1): accept valid alternative wording and do not penalise a missing accent unless it changes the meaning. Total is out of 13 (5 auto + 3 + 3 + 2). Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 80 words.
